main_text.p: ætherei folarium radiorum ignis particula cum vitriolo in unum coalescat, (ficut ad oculum patet, inquit, quando antimonium per speculum ardens calcinatur; nam quasi ad dimidium pondus ejus augetur:) Atque in hoc casu luminosæ hujus substantiæ pars, quæ in vitriolo ita calcinato remanet, maxime erit disposità quæ à simili luce ac radiis solaribus in aëre elevetur: ficuti videmus, quod quando, ut antlia melius aquam ex puteo exantlet, efficere animus est, prius parum aquæ furfum injiciamus: Lux itaque cùm substantiam sibi connaturalem facile auferat, longè adhuc facilius id quod sibi adsimilatum est, secum unà abripit, & deportat. 4. Hi radii solares, inquit, unum cum Vitriolo corpus constituentes, majorem & præstantiorem adhuc ipsi virtutem, quàm antea obtinuerat, communicare conciliareque possunt; æquè ac oculis cernimus, antimonium sole calcinatum, vim venenatam,

The text at the top right is partially cut, and the header "De Pulvere" is set in small capitals; the transcription above follows the visible letters. Bottom of page: no catchword or signature visible. Possible misreadings: "dispositâ", "substantiam", "adsimilatum" are uncertain and may be rendered slightly differently in print.
